results.title: Pikuniku (2024)
results.brief_description:
Cute, colourful and a little bit chaotic, Pikuniku is a puzzle adventure where even walking can make you laugh.

Play as Piku, a wobbly red creature who helps a village fight back against robots stealing its natural resources. Solve puzzles, explore strange places and kick almost anything in sight. Grab a second controller and team up as Piku and Niku for special two-player challenges.

Created by a small independent team, Pikuniku hides a rebellious story beneath its simple shapes and bright colours. Its title even sounds like the Japanese word for “picnic”. Keep an eye out for Pikuniku 2 in 2027.

results.title: Neva (2024)
results.brief_description:
What happens when someone you protect grows up and starts protecting you?

In Neva, warrior Alba and a young wolf must survive together as their beautiful world is slowly overtaken by dark forces. Players run, jump, solve puzzles and battle enemies as the pair travel through the changing landscape. At first, the cub depends on Alba for everything. As the seasons pass, she grows into a powerful wolf with a mind of her own.

Created by Barcelona’s Nomada Studio, Neva combines action and adventure with delicate, hand-painted-looking landscapes. Its story of love, growing up and letting go has moved players around the world – and earned the game international awards, including a BAFTA.

Trevor Lunn interviews children’s writer Alison Lester about her children’s books particularly “Clive eats alligators”. She dicusses with children from South Melbourne Primary School her reasons and inspirations for writing and the choice of illustrations in her childrens’ books.

results.title: Home of the brave
results.creator_credit: Roger Scholes, Katherine Scholes, Edward Street Films, Film Victoria and Victoria. Disability Services Division
results.brief_description: Provides an historical overview of the evolution of models for the care of the intellectually disabled; from the institutions of the early 1800’s through to current the community living options. The strength of the institutions is acknowledged but the real restrictions on quality of life are highlighted. Examines issues surrounding people with an intellectual disability moving from institutions into the community, especially the nature and extent of support services. Accompanied by a 3p. Study Guide inside the cover.

results.title: Report on wheat
results.creator_credit: Roy A. Driver and Herschells Films
results.brief_description: A survey of Victoria’s second largest industry - the production of wheat. Stresses the need for increased production to meet the requirement of local and overseas buyers. Shows the work being done by the State Research Farm, the Victorian Department of Agriculture and the agricultural colleges in this direction; the checking of flour for quality; the breeding, growing and harvesting of wheat varieties; the development of improved wheat strains; bread manufacture; the bulk handling of wheat at rail heads and storage depots.

results.title: This is my home
results.creator_credit: Roy A. Driver and Herschells Films
results.brief_description: Care and accommodation for the elderly in Victoria; shows the variety of specially planned homes available - individual houses with gardens in selectged areas; units of ten self-contained flats; flatettes with a community lounge; large homes with a matron presiding; small hospitals where patients are encouraged to walk again. Also stresses the importance of practising handicrafts, hobbies and gardening and being generally active.

results.title: Frog Detective 1: The Haunted Island
results.brief_description:
In Frog Detective 1: The Haunted Island, the stereotype of a hard-boiled detective becomes a friendly frog investigating a ghostly noise. Developed by Grace Bruxner while she was still studying game design, this first game in the Frog Detective trilogy turns detective fiction into a silly, kind-hearted adventure.
It borrows from screen mysteries like Agatha Christie’s Poirot (1989), using familiar music, camera angles and episodic structure. But the mystery is deliberately low-stakes, and the detective is polite, enthusiastic and apologetic when suspicious. Through comic dialogue and absurd interviews, Bruxner finds humour in making noir softer, stranger and much more charming.

constellations_other.name: Animal hijinks
constellations_other.description: As long as stories have been told on screen, audiences have loved films, TV shows, memes and videogames about animals being naughty. This constellation shares some key examples of animal comedy throughout the ages.

results.title: The Dance of the angels: ceramic sculptures of John Perceval
results.creator_credit: Tim Burstall, Patrick Ryan and Eltham Films
results.brief_description: Camera movement and film editing are combined to animate the ceramic figurines of John Perceval. He created his angels “more or less as symbols of the world’s survival.” An intangible element common to all Perceval’s angels is their spirit of humanity. These ceramic sculptures are disting- uished by their beautiful modelling, and their lustrous red copper glaze with its uncanny depth and beauty. Perceval does not devote himself exclusively to ceramic sculpture; he gives equal time to painting and has won the McCaughey and Vizard-Whollohan Prizes, and shared the Wynne Prize in 1961. Photography by Gerard Vanderberg; music by Dorian Le Gallienne.

results.title: City on the Swan
results.creator_credit: Norman A. Uren and Western Australian Government Film Unit
results.brief_description:
Promotional tourism film presented by the Western Australian Tourist Development Authority and produced by the Western Australian Government Film Unit. The film showcases Perth through its architecture, industry, transport, recreation and tourist attractions, presenting the city as a modern urban centre organised around the Swan River.

City scenes include St Georges Terrace, London Court, Wellington Street, the Hotel Adelphi, the Old Barracks, Narrows Bridge and Canning Bridge. Sequences at the General Post Office show radio telephone and postal services, while footage of factories and manufacturing includes porcelain and domestic pottery production, woodworking and the manufacture of period and modern furniture using plastics and metals.

The film follows Perth from the end of the working week into the weekend. On Friday evening, factory and city workers leave work as peak-hour traffic, buses and rail services carry commuters from the city to the suburbs and surrounding areas.

Saturday is presented through sport and recreation, including Australian rules football (footage of match between West Coast Eagles and North Melbourne teams), cricket, golf, rowing, motor racing, horse racing, water skiing (footage of women synchronised on skis) and the “novelty and brilliance of the marching girls”.
Tourist and civic sites include Queens Gardens with its Peter Pan statue, black swans at Hyde Park, the museum displays at the Old Mill in South Perth, (Princess) May Drive in Kings Park, and the University of Western Australia (footage of Winthrop Hall’s reflection pond and bust of Socrates). Also includes an excursion to Yanchep which features boating, gardens, swimming and afternoon tea.

Perth’s nightlife is represented through drive-in cinemas, including footage of projectionists at work, and the Ambassadors Theatre on Hay Street (demolished 1972).

On Sunday, focus returns to the Swan River, with fishing along Riverside Drive, speedboats and yacht racing on the river. The film concludes by promoting Perth as the “City on the Swan”, defined by the river, outdoor recreation and a relaxed metropolitan lifestyle (“Gentle and gracious, Perth makes its appeal with a delightful flare as the City on the Swan.”)
